blocks.text: Lucy Letby - Cross-examination Day 5: Babies H & I
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Thursday, 25 May 2023
(In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Overnight have you thought of anything that you have previously said that you would like to amend or add extra detail to?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: The only thing -- you asked me yesterday if the Datix had been completed about the chest drains and I can confirm it was done.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. And that's by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you remember doing that, do you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You remember doing that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have seen the Datix on the system.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We had got to count 10, which I can see from here is still open on the desk in front of you. I don't know whether the jury have it. It's behind divider 1 in jury bundle 1. This is an allegation of attempted murder on 26 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You were, of course, on duty on the night shift of the 25th into the 26th, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And I'd like to start, if we may, with the population distribution chart, which is in the [Baby H] sequence at tile 177.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Video feed to court disrupted)
I think if you just rewind one question and go back over it just in case -- I don't know whether it did -- I'm not following the transcript.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I have the transcript here and there are actually two issues that I've raised that haven't been transcribed so I'll deal with them both if I may.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Just so that you understand, Ms Letby, the audiovideo link to the transcription service was lost whilst I was asking you questions.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So I'm just going to deal with the issues that are missing from the transcript. The first was -- I was asking you whether the staffing levels had in any way, in your view, contributed to [Baby H]'s collapse on this shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The second was whether somebody's medical incompetence had contributed in any way to [Baby H]'s collapse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I think potentially with the management of her chest drains, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And by management, what do you mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The insertion of them and how they were secured.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. What is it about the insertion of them that you suggest was deficient?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm not saying it was deficient, but I think it has been accepted that there were issues with the drains throughout the trial. It's come to light.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's not the question. The question, if you wouldn't mind, is what are you suggesting it was about the management, the insertion, to use --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That they may not have been correct because there was a lot of discussion needed on how to insert the drains.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Does it come to this then, because you are saying there was a lot of discussion amongst the doctors about inserting the drains, that means that there is a problem with the drains?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Potentially, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: May I just confirm one matter --
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Because I took a note before we went offline and the note I have was in answer to the question about the competence, the answer we got was:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "There was potential incompetence with regard to the location of the chest drains and how they were secured."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That was what was said before we went offline and certainly that's the note I have, so it's important that although the transcript didn't get that the first time round I note that that is what Ms Letby said in answer to that question at the beginning.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So that I can understand, we can all understand what you are suggesting, what are you suggesting was the problem?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That potentially [Baby H]'s pneumothoraces were not treated appropriately.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. And that is because of what?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lack of experience and using multiple drains of different types that nobody seemed particularly confident to use.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Which particular doctor or doctors are you suggesting lacked the experience required?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Multiple doctors.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, yes, but --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Dr Harkness. Dr Jayaram. Dr Gibbs. Dr Ventress even, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Now, can we go back to tile 27, please? This is something that you dealt with in answer to questions from your own counsel some time ago now. We can see that it's dated a couple of days earlier, on 24 September at 09.15.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just so that we can understand the connection or the relevance or potential relevance of this text sent by you to your friend [Nurse E], are you suggesting there was anything unsafe going on in the unit on the shift that we are dealing with now? In other words, the shift that began on the 25th into 26 September.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, this is referring to a different time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So it's not relevant, is that right, to [Baby H]'s collapse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, because she was one-to-one nursed at that point.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Now, a short time ago when I was asking you about your friend [Nurse A], and I was making the point with you that she was truly supernumerary, you suggested that she was in some way responsible for helping you with [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What are you suggesting about her function on --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That the role of a supernumerary shift leader is to support staff on the unit with medications and anything that would need to be done, and particularly with [Baby H] I was unfamiliar with chest drains and [Nurse A] played a part in assisting me with [Baby H]'s care.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Did you not have experience of chest drains?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not a lot of experience, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I thought you said you'd dealt with them at Liverpool.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have, yes, but I'd not had a lot of experience with them at the Countess of Chester, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you suggest to anybody at the beginning of this particular shift that in some way your knowledge or experience was deficient?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. I don't think it was deficient. I think it was raised that I didn't have a lot of experience and part of that was that [Nurse A] was supernumerary and would be able to assist me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what are the tasks with which she was assisting you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I can't recall specifically now, but it would have been medications and I know when she had further chest drains put in, [Nurse A] helped with the insertion and setting-up of those drains with me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Let's deal with those two issues then.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Medication she'd have to co-sign with you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Somebody would have had to have co-signed medication with me, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And that would be true of any child, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So there's nothing exceptional about [Baby H] in that respect?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So far as the insertion of a chest drain was concerned, which particular chest drain are you suggesting she assisted you with?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The drain that was inserted on the night of the 26th.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, this is Dr Gibbs' chest drain; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So this was at 02.15; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I don't know the time right now, but...
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I think there are two times in the documents: one is 02.10, one is 02.15, in the early hours of the 26th.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What I would like you to concentrate on, if you would, please, is -- that was after [Baby H] had collapsed, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what I'm interested in asking you about, and what the jury may be interested in, is what led to her collapse. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So let's concentrate on that time if we can, so between 20.00 hours and 02.00 hours or thereabouts.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We've got a period of about 6 hours, give or take; yes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Does it come to this, that so far as the assistance you were getting from [Nurse A] was concerned, that was limited to co-signing for medications?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say without reviewing the charts.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, have you looked -- you clearly looked at the charts last night because you raised an issue when I asked you to clarify anything you've already said.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Have you looked at the charts overnight?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, but I can't remember every detail and I think it would be unrealistic if I could remember every single detail.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, you tell -- you see, it's your case that she was in that -- you said in answer to your own counsel, or you gave the impression, that she was in nursery 1 with you, helping you with [Baby H] all the time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I did not say she was there at all times, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What are you saying so we understand?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That [Nurse A] was supernumerary and she did help me throughout the evening. I can't be specific at what time or what she actually did at certain times but she was with me on and off throughout the shift.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And that would all be documented on the charts, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not all of it, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, what sort of thing wouldn't --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If she's with me to give verbal advice or if she's helping me do something that I have then signed for on the chart it would not necessarily have her signature.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But she gave me a lot of verbal advice that night.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: About what?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: About the management of [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: In particular in what respect?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In management of her chest drains. And then when she collapsed, it was information about baptism and things like that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: For the time being, let's concentrate on what caused [Baby H] to collapse; all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's not worry about what happened after she collapsed for now. Do you remember that [Baby H] collapsed in the early hours of the 26th?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall specific details. I know she did collapse, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember hearing the evidence of [Father of Baby H], who is [Baby H]'s father?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not in detail, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, it was read to the jury by agreement on 18 January this year. And of course, this is a statement that you have had available to you for a couple of years now, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. What [Father of Baby H] said -- and I'm going to read to you directly from his statement; all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: He was talking about his daughter and he said:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "She was in an incubator and was on CPAP to help her breathe. So we spent time in there from Tuesday onwards and on the Friday..."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And we're talking about a Friday, aren't we, 25 September?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "... on the Friday, I'd been there late with [Mother of Baby H]'s mum."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Mother of Baby H]'s mum is [Father of Baby H]'s mother-in-law given [Mother of Baby H] is his wife:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I'd been there late with [Mother of Baby H]'s mum [on Friday] until about midnight and we'd come back to the house and I was awoken by her in the early hours."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's [Father of Baby H]'s agreed evidence that on this shift, for which we saw the population distribution at tile 177, he was there until just before midnight or thereabouts.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember what time the doctors were called to [Baby H]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That night for the first time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just before midnight, at 23.50.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I would like to look at your nursing note for this occasion. It's tile 208, please. Given that it's your note, would you read it through for us to remind yourself of what it was you wrote?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Written for care given from 20.00 to present. Emergency equipment checked, fluids calculated. [Baby H] nursed in an incubator, ventilated with size 3.5 ET tube, 8 centimetres at lips. Ventilator settings gradually increased during shift in line with blood gas and clinical picture: currently 24/4,
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: inspiratory time 0.45, rate 60 in 28% oxygen. x2 chest drains in situ at start of shift. Intermittently swinging. Serous fluid ++ accumulating.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "23.30. Bradycardia and desaturation requiring Neopuff in 100% to recover. 10ml [I assume that's air] aspirated from chest drain by Registrar Ventress. Following poor blood gas and 100% oxygen requirement, Consultant Gibbs attended the unit and inserted a third chest drain."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's just stop it there because that takes us up to and including the time of the first desaturation and indeed the second desaturation when Dr Gibbs was called to help. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we look at the time that you created that record, please. Can you confirm that you began to write it at 04.14 and you closed it at 04.28?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And I am going to suggest to you that you misrepresented the time of this event; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So I'm going to suggest this is another occasion where you have deliberately misrepresented the facts; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is an event that happened just before midnight, at about 23.50, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall. From my notes there I've said 23.30.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where would you have got that information from when you wrote it down at 04.14?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Either notes that I've made myself or any medical records --
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- or anything on the charts relevant to that time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We've seen many medical records, haven't we --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- written in varying degrees of legibility by varying medical practitioners?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And they were available on paper for you to consult if there was any doubt in your mind about when something had happened?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Dr Ventress, for it was she who was called at 23.50, had made a note and you could have looked at it and used it to create your own note, couldn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At the time, if she had written the note prior to this, then yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Let's see what you were writing on the manuscript notes because these will be relevant as well.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can go to tile 199, please. I'd like to concentrate on the material in the left-hand side of the page if we can. This actually should be material that the jury has in jury bundle 2. If you'd like to look at a paper copy, you will find it behind divider 10.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The page number, as we can see on the screen, is 12701. Would you prefer a paper copy or are you happy with the screen?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I'd prefer to see it on the screen, thank you.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. The utility of the paper copy in these circumstances may be to tie in the times with the entries, okay? Do you understand what I mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Because in order to read what's on the screen it may be, for people like me, we're going to have to magnify what you have written and that will obliterate the corresponding time at the top of the screen. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'd like to start, with Mr Murphy's assistance, please, with your entries, which are the four in the left-hand half of the page to the right-hand edge of that half.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can turn them through 90 degrees as well, Mr Murphy, clockwise, then it may facilitate us being able to read them.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we see the first entry that you made as being at 21.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The second in the 22.00 hours column?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What does that read, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "22.10. Desat 52% during..."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Heel prick"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yeah:
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "... heel prick. SHO present. Serous fluid ++. x2 drains."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, "SHO present". Who was the SHO that you were referring to here?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall from memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, there was an SHO on duty that night called Jessica Burke.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We saw it in the -- we can see it at tile 177.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry, not Jessica Burke, Jessica Scott, I beg your pardon, Jessica Scott.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The SHO wasn't present, was she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's what I've written there.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there a note in the medical notes from the SHO about this desaturation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Oh, I think you do. There isn't, is there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Serous fluid ++, x2 drain."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You then write in the 23.00 hours column:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Blood commenced 23.05."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that your writing as well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then in the midnight column:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Brady/desat 23.30."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "10ml air aspirated from..."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Flutter drain."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "... from flutter drain."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then there's an upward arrow?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, it's increased the ventilator pressure to 24/4.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then to the right of that what does it say in the next box?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Clear."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: All of the writing?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You interpret whether you do them individually as different boxes or as a unit, the totality of that material.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't see without looking at the columns. I'm assuming it's clear either orally or -- I can't see the column it
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: represents. But there's small blood -- "small bloodstained" and then beneath that it says "clear".
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Is it "plus clear"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Plus small bloodstained plus clear."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But I'm not sure which column that refers to.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's all in the -- we're looking at things sideways on now, whereas this is a vertical column. This is why it helps to look at the paper copy at the same time so that we can orientate what we're looking at. This is all in the midnight column.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I'm talking about the row that would be on the lefthand side, I think, where it indicates if it's OP -- here we are, "suction". The top bit is:
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Suction on ET produced plus small bloodstained. Oropharyngeal was plus clear."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's looking into the mouth is clear?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The airway was clear, I've had clear fluid.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So here we have another child under your care who's producing bloodstained secretions in their throat; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think if it's come from the ET tube, it wouldn't necessarily be the throat. If the ET tube is in the lungs, I presume it's from there.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Had you interfered with [Baby H]'s ET tube?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Moved it around a bit to destabilise her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can we look at your defence statement, please, to try and put this into a bit more context. Have you got the document?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, it's here.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is paragraph 101, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What did you write of these events on this night?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I don't recall any specific episode of desaturation during the night shift of the 25th into the 26 September."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. You then go on, I think, as we established yesterday, to say that the following night, the 26th to the 27th, [Baby H] deteriorated rapidly and you were with [Nurse A].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that date is not correct.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No, okay. Is that actually a reference to this night, the 25th to the 26th?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And to be fair to you, you then say at 103:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "In my memory, both nights merge into one. I cannot be specific about what I did during either of the collapses."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then you talk about the baby LO that we dealt with yesterday and to whom we will come in due course.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Of course, just going back to your note at 22.10, if a baby with two chest drains in, as [Baby H] was, had really desaturated to 52%, that would be potentially a serious medical issue, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
